```text
I think it's helpful for those thinking how to implement this (unless, you'd like to give it a try), if you provide some more detail. 

For example: 
1. How would you implement this? If you don't know how you would do it programmatically, you could describe the "high-level" vision of how this would work. For example, as a Calendso user you can currently create different event types of various durations — you can then decide which event type to send the link to. Thus, would you have a completely separate "customisable duration event type", which is the only event type that for which duration can be changed? What's your vision?
2. I might be misunderstanding what you are saying, but an "inviter" is the person inviting, and "invitee" is the person being invited — if you send your Calendso link to someone, then you are the inviter, and the person you are sending it to, an invitee. Therefore, by saying "[I want to] let the inviter set the meeting duration/ending time" - do you mean "invitee"? Since you can already can do that as an inviter (the person sending the invite) — you create different event types as a Calendso user and thus implicitly set the duration of those events when creating an event type and sending off the link. 

Apologies if misunderstood what you said but if you can clarify then I can start thinking about the ways in which this could be accomplished and perhaps ask you for some additional clarification. 
--

I like this idea. I'm not sure if Calendly has this feature.

From a UX perspective, here's how I think it would work:
1. For a specific or every Friday, 1pm-5pm are my 1:1 "office hours" for my students (invitees). I select that they can schedule a block of 15, 30 or 60 minutes depending on their need (I would think these 3 would be the top 3 options available and in demand, with 20 min and 50 min being the 2 other timeframes that I would recommend being options for the inviter's UI)
2. Invitee goes to meeting booking screen in Calendso, select the date of interest
3. Here's where the UI would differ: Invitee is asked if they'd like a 15, 30, or 60 minute meeting
4. the UI provides meeting start times at 15 minute intervals such that the 15, 30, or 60 minute meeting would end within the 1-5pm time frame
5. Same UI moving forward for booking meetings as with regular meeting.

Future features: ability for invitee to return to start of booking process if invitee wants to change the meeting duration to longer or shorter.

Let me know if I'm misinterpreting this.

author:	aspiers
association:	contributor

> have an event type for 15min, 30min and one for 60min (that's how all scheduling tools do it)

Unfortunately this is not a good solution.  I already tried that as a workaround in the past, and it was a massive pain.  For example, let's say I want the following event types:

- Personal video call for non-work topics
- In-person meeting for personal topics
- Work video call with colleagues within my company
- Work video call with external particpants outside my company

All of these need their own event type, because they all require different parameters.  However I want to give anyone requesting any of these types of meetings a choice of different time durations.  (The "office hours" scenario mentioned above is one of several great reasons why this can be needed.)  If those choices are limited to, say, 30 / 60 / 90 mins, then that multiplies the four event types above by 3, so I have to create 12 event types in total.  If I also want to allow other durations like 15 mins or 120 mins then it gets even worse.

> in my experience its quite rare that the same event type has different durations.

I can of course appreciate that this is your experience, but it doesn't mean that many other people have different needs.  If you want to cater to the huge addressable market for calendar apps then I believe this is the kind of flexibility a lot of people will find useful. 

So I would be super grateful if you could reconsider this feature request.  I know that some of your competitors don't offer this feature, but that's a great opportunity for Cal to differentiate itself and become even more awesome ;-)
--

[**@PeerRich**](https://github.com/PeerRich) commented on [March 19, 2022 11:39 PM](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/issues/88#issuecomment-1073130620 "2022-03-19T23:39:59Z - Replied by Github Reply Comments"):
> can you recommend your favorite way you'd want this to be implemented?

Thanks a lot for the quick response and for being open-minded on this!  I think the implementation could be very simple:

1. When creating a new event type, multiple durations are allowed, e.g. add a `+` (plus) icon to add extra durations, and a trash icon to remove them.  Or allow comma-separated values like `15,30,60` as a more quick and dirty implementation.
2. When using an event type link to book a slot, if the event type has multiple durations, then the person booking the event has to first choose a duration before proceeding as normal with the rest of the booking process.  Then the availability will be displayed according to that chosen event duration.
3. Make it easy (i.e. ideally with a single click) for the person booking to change their duration choice after selection, in which case the displayed availability is adjusted accordingly. So for example if they are looking for an hour slot but can't find any availability which works for them, they have the option of reducing the slot to 30 mins in order to potentially gain more options.
4. [Stretch goal for optimal UX] If the event type allows multiple durations, then after the user of the link selects a duration and a day, if there are no slots available for that combination, do one of the following:
    - If there are smaller slots available on that day, rather than just displaying "All booked today", display something like "No 60 minute slots today, but there are two 30 minute slots." and a button "__Reduce duration to 30 minutes__" which changes the duration parameter and updates the display accordingly.
    - If there are *no* smaller slots available on that day, display something like "No slots of any duration available today".  (Just keeping the original "All booked today" text would also be OK, but I was thinking that this change might clarify the situation a bit better in this case.)

I also note that there seems to be some terminology confusion here which we should try to clear up:

[**@harad**](https://github.com/harad) commented on [April 22, 2021 9:43 PM](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/issues/88#issuecomment-825172079 "2021-04-22T20:43:30Z - Replied by Github Reply Comments"):
> 2.  I might be misunderstanding what you are saying, but an "inviter" is the person inviting, and "invitee" is the person being invited — if you send your Calendso link to someone, then you are the inviter, and the person you are sending it to, an invitee.

That seems the exact opposite of what I'd expect, and therefore quite confusing.  In my mind, the person who receives the link and uses it to request a meeting is the one trying to set up the meeting, and therefore they are the inviter, and the owner of the cal.com account and link is the invitee.  In other words, "I am using your cal.com link to invite you to a meeting".

Perhaps this confusion stems from the fact that an event link can either result in an immediate booking, or it can result in an invite which requires confirmation.  In the former case, I can see an argument for describing the link sender (i.e. cal.com account holder) as the "inviter", since they are inviting the counterparty to book their time.  But in the latter case, the link sender is "inviting the other party to create an invite"!

> Therefore, by saying "\[I want to\] let the inviter set the meeting duration/ending time" - do you mean "invitee"? Since you can already can do that as an inviter (the person sending the invite) — you create different event types as a Calendso user and thus implicitly set the duration of those events when creating an event type and sending off the link.

Since the original description begins with the words "As a Calendso user who is invited to meet with the inviter", it seems very clear to me that this is not what is being asked for, and that @kimjin8 and I both think of the Calendso user being the "invitee" and the person using the link as the "inviter".  It is well understood that an event type can already be customised to a single, fixed duration, but this issue is requesting more than that, i.e. that the duration of the event type can be flexible.
--

> 
> Since the original description begins with the words "As a Calendso user who is invited to meet with the inviter", it seems very clear to me that this is not what is being asked for, and that @kimjin8 and I both think of the Calendso user being the "invitee" and the person using the link as the "inviter". It is well understood that an event type can already be customised to a single, fixed duration, but this issue is requesting more than that, i.e. that the duration of the event type can be flexible.

@aspiers whilst I appreciate your argument, I still think that the cal.com's user is the inviter, and the person receiving the link would be the invitee. Since the link originates with the inviter, not the invitee. Ultimately, it's the person with the greater control over the link and the available times for the meeting should be the inviter. 

The inviter, the cal.com's user, is streamlining the process of scheduling a meeting with them, and therefore, makes a link available. Interesting take on: 'In other words, "I am using your cal.com link to invite you to a meeting"'. - I would argue it's the right opposite, and your example is very specific. Whilst it's true in some cases and probably largely depends on the way you use cal.com, I use cal.com to simply reduce back-and-forth, even when I'm the one asking the person for a meeting - therefore, for me, it'd be more of "I am asking you to use my cal.com link to invite you to a meeting". As in, I am providing you with my cal.com link, so we can have a meeting at a mutually convenient time. If you send a birthday party invitation, who is the inviter, and who is the invitee? The person whose birthday we are celebrating, or the person who is attending the party? I'd strongly argue it's the former, not the latter. 

Whilst I don't have the data to back it up to what most people think - I think potentially changing the meaning of inviter/invitee could lead to some serious confusion among the users. Happy to be proved wrong.  
--

Thanks @harad, I do see your points.  Ultimately both perspectives have validity, and it's not a matter of one being right and the other being wrong.  In case you have any doubts about that, please consider this scenario:

1. I have a conversation with a friend or colleague, either online or offline, in which I mention that if they ever need to talk to me about anything, they are welcome to book a time slot via the given cal.com URL.  They make a note of this URL for future use.
2. Six months later, they visit this URL to book a time slot.  An email automatically appears in my inbox asking me to confirm whether I am OK with that time slot.  I confirm, and the meeting happens.
3. Six months later, the same thing happens again.

In this scenario, they are much closer to being the inviter than I am, since I never requested organisation of a specific event; I merely expressed my openness to being available, should they wish to meet with me.  On both occasions, they were the one who initially proposed the meeting.  Cal.com was merely the tool to facilitate this process in an efficient manner, but I could have equally said "look, if you ever want to talk, just send me an email and we'll find a time we're both free".

But anyway, let's not get too distracted into a long debate on the semantics ;-) That would not be very productive, and it's certainly off topic for this particular GitHub issue.  There are two concrete takeaways here:

1. It seems very clear that the OP was using "inviter" to refer to the person using the link to book a time slot.
2. As a more general point, it's important that cal.com uses clear wording to avoid any confusion along these lines.  I believe the wording I have seen so far has been perfectly clear, so I'm not aware of anything actionable on that front.
```

```text
## User Story
As a user, I want to quickly book another meeting with someone from a past booking so that I do not have to manually re-enter their information.

## User Scenario
When viewing a past booking, the user can choose to book another meeting with the same attendee. The application starts a new booking flow and automatically fills in the attendee's existing name and email. The user can then choose a new date and time and complete the booking normally. The original booking remains unchanged because booking again creates a separate booking rather than rescheduling the previous one.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Add a **"Book Again"** action to past bookings.
2. Clicking "Book Again" starts a new booking flow rather than modifying or rescheduling the original booking.
3. Automatically prefill the previous attendee's:
   - Name
   - Email
4. Allow the user to review or edit the prefilled attendee information before confirming the new booking.
5. Allow the user to select a new available date and time using the existing booking flow.
6. Successfully completing the flow creates a new booking while leaving the original booking unchanged.
7. Add or update tests to verify the rebooking behavior and ensure existing booking and rescheduling functionality continues to work.

## Out of Scope
- Building a People view of previous attendees.
- Displaying meeting counts or previous meeting history.
- Changing the existing rescheduling workflow.
- Automatically selecting a new meeting date or time.

## User Story
As a user, I want to see the people I have previously met with so that I can review my meeting history and easily schedule another meeting with them.

## User Scenario
The system uses the user's previous bookings to create a People view containing the attendees they have met with. Instead of showing the same person multiple times, each attendee appears once with useful information about their meeting history, including how many times they have met and their most recent meeting. From this view, the user can start the Book Again flow for that person.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Add a **People** view that displays attendees from the user's previous bookings.
2. Display each attendee's:
   - Name
   - Email
   - Number of previous meetings
   - Most recent meeting date
3. Display an attendee only once when multiple previous bookings exist with the same person.
4. Calculate the total number of previous meetings for each attendee.
5. Determine and display the most recent meeting date for each attendee.
6. Add a **"Book Again"** action for each person that uses the rebooking functionality created in the first sub-issue.
7. Display an appropriate empty state when the user does not have any previous attendees.
8. Add or update tests to verify attendee grouping, meeting counts, most recent meeting dates, and the People view behavior.

## Out of Scope
- Creating a separate contacts or address book system.
- Allowing users to manually add people who have never had a booking.
- Editing an attendee's personal information from the People view.
- Changing existing bookings or rescheduling behavior.
```

## #51: Add a rebook feature (parent, effort:low, 0/2 sub-issues done)
**Problem:** cal.diy forgets everyone once a booking ends.
**Proposal:** Add a "Book again" action on past bookings that pre-fills the attendee. Add a **People** view showing who you've met, how often, when you last met, and a one-click way to schedule the next meeting. The issue stresses that this is **different from reschedule**.
**User story:** "As someone with recurring 1:1s, I want to rebook last month's person without retyping their name and email."

## #87: Add the rebook button and functionality (effort:low)
**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Add a **"Book Again"** action to past bookings.
2. It starts a **new** booking flow and does not modify or reschedule the original.
3. It pre-fills the previous attendee's **name and email**.
4. The user can review and edit the pre-filled info before confirming.
5. The user picks a new date and time through the existing booking flow.
6. Completing the flow creates a new booking and leaves the original unchanged.
7. Add or update tests for rebooking, and make sure existing booking and rescheduling still work.

**Out of scope:** the People view, meeting counts or history, changes to rescheduling, and picking a date automatically.

## #88: Create the "People" view for easy rebooking (effort:medium)
**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Add a **People** view of attendees from the user's past bookings.
2. Show each attendee's **name, email, number of previous meetings, and most recent meeting date**.
3. Each attendee appears once, even if there are several bookings with them.
4. Calculate each attendee's total meeting count.
5. Find and show each attendee's most recent meeting date.
6. Give each person a **"Book Again"** action that reuses the rebooking from #87.
7. Show an empty state when the user has no previous attendees.
8. Add tests for grouping, counts, most-recent dates, and the view's behavior.

**Out of scope:** a separate contacts or address book, adding people manually, editing attendee info, and changes to bookings or rescheduling.

**Order:** #87 has to come first, because #88's "Book Again" action depends on it.

You're mostly right, and I overstated it. The two mostly don't depend on each other. There's one point where they connect.

**What's independent:** almost all of #88. The People view, grouping attendees, meeting counts, most-recent dates and the empty state only read past bookings, and none of that needs #87. Likewise, #87 doesn't need #88 at all.

**The one link:** #88's criterion 6 says:
> Add a "Book Again" action for each person that uses the rebooking functionality created in the first sub-issue.

So only the People view's "Book Again" button reuses #87's work. #87 starts a booking flow with the attendee's name and email pre-filled. If that logic lives in one small shared helper, the People view just calls it.

**What this means in practice:** you can build them in parallel or in either order. If you do #88 first, leave the "Book Again" button out, or stub it, and wire it up once #87's helper exists. You don't have to finish #87 before starting #88.

Start with **#87**. Here's why:

- **It's smaller.** It's labeled `effort:low`, compared with `effort:medium` for #88. It's basically one action on past bookings plus pre-filling name and email in the existing booking flow, so you can get a PR merged early in the sprint.
- **It builds the shared piece.** The "start a booking with this attendee pre-filled" helper is what #88's button needs. If you build it first, #88 can call it directly, with no stub to come back to later.
- **It's lower risk.** It reuses the existing booking flow. #88 needs new design decisions: where the People view lives, how to group attendees (probably by email), and how to make the counts and dates queries efficient. You'll make those calls better once you've worked through the booking data in #87.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-09 02:25:08Z)**_

I have enough to plan #87. The existing code already does most of the work.

## How it works today
- **Booking actions** are built in `apps/web/components/booking/actions/bookingActions.ts`. There's an "After event" group (`getAfterEventActions`, around L183) that already holds past-booking actions like no-show and charge card. **Book Again belongs there.**
- **The booking page already pre-fills from the URL.** `useInitialFormValues.ts` (L135-138) reads `?name=` and `?email=`, and those values override the logged-in user's details. That matters because the organizer is the one clicking.
- **The dropdown needs no changes.** An action with only an `href` already renders as a link (`BookingActionsDropdown.tsx` L611).

## Plan
1. **Shared helper** in a new file, `apps/web/modules/bookings/lib/buildBookAgainUrl.ts`. This is the piece #88 will reuse. Given an event type, its owner and an attendee, it returns:
   - `/team/{team.slug}/{slug}?name=…&email=…` for team events
   - `/{username}/{slug}?name=…&email=…` otherwise
   - `null` if there's no event type, slug or username, so the action can't be offered

   It's a small, plain function that builds no URL to the external site. There's an existing helper, `buildEventUrlFromBooking`, but it's async and expects org/profile fields the bookings list doesn't load. Organizations are removed in this edition anyway.
2. **Add the action** to `getAfterEventActions`: `{ id: "book_again", icon: "calendar-plus", label: t("book_again"), href }`.
3. **Add a `book_again` case** to `isActionDisabled` so the action is disabled when the booking isn't in the past or the helper returned `null`.
4. **Add the translation** `"book_again": "Book again"` to `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`.
5. **Tests:**
   - unit tests for the helper: user event, team event, missing slug, and special characters in name or email
   - new cases in `bookingActions.test.ts` (the `getAfterEventActions` block, L436): shown for past bookings, disabled for upcoming ones, and the href is correct

That's about 5 files and well under the PR size limit. Reschedule and the original booking aren't touched, which covers acceptance criteria 2 and 6.

## Three things to decide before coding
- **Which attendee?** A booking can have several. I'd pre-fill the first one (the person who booked) and leave per-attendee options to the People view in #88.
- **Criterion 4 (editable pre-fill):** `useShouldBeDisabledDueToPrefill.tsx` may make URL-filled fields read-only. I'll check this in the real app. If they come out locked, it needs a fix.
- **Cancelled past bookings:** should Book Again show for them too? I'd say yes, since you still met (or meant to meet) that person.

If you're fine with first attendee and yes on cancelled, I'll make the changes. I'll leave committing to you.

```text
229	export function isActionDisabled(actionId: string, context: BookingActionContext): boolean {
230	  const {
231	    booking,
232	    isBookingInPast,
233	    isDisabledRescheduling,
234	    isDisabledCancelling,
235	    isAttendee,
236	    isCancelled,
237	    isRejected,
238	  } = context;
239	
240	  switch (actionId) {
241	    case "reschedule":
242	    case "reschedule_request":
243	      // Only apply minimum reschedule notice restriction if user is NOT the organizer
244	      // If user is an attendee (or not authenticated), apply the restriction
245	      const isUserOrganizer =
246	        !isAttendee &&
247	        booking.loggedInUser?.userId &&
248	        booking.user?.id &&
249	        booking.loggedInUser.userId === booking.user.id;
250	      const isWithinMinimumNotice =
251	        !isUserOrganizer &&
252	        isWithinMinimumRescheduleNotice(
253	          new Date(booking.startTime),
254	          booking.eventType.minimumRescheduleNotice ?? null
255	        );
256	      return (
257	        isCancelled ||
258	        isRejected ||
259	        (isBookingInPast && !booking.eventType.allowReschedulingPastBookings) ||
260	        isDisabledRescheduling ||
261	        isWithinMinimumNotice
262	      );
263	    case "cancel":
264	      return isDisabledCancelling || isBookingInPast || isCancelled || isRejected;
265	    case "view_recordings":
266	      return !(isBookingInPast && booking.status === BookingStatus.ACCEPTED && context.isCalVideoLocation);
267	    case "meeting_session_details":
268	      return !(isBookingInPast && booking.status === BookingStatus.ACCEPTED && context.isCalVideoLocation);
269	    case "charge_card":
270	      return context.cardCharged;
271	    case "reassign":
272	    case "change_location":
273	    case "add_members":
274	      return isBookingInPast || isCancelled || isRejected;
275	    default:
276	      return false;
277	  }
278	}
279	
280	export function getActionLabel(actionId: string, context: BookingActionContext): string {
281	  const { isTabRecurring, isRecurring, attendeeList, cardCharged, t } = context;
282	
283	  switch (actionId) {
284	    case "reject":
285	      return (isTabRecurring || context.isTabUnconfirmed) && isRecurring ? t("reject_all") : t("reject");
286	    case "confirm":
287	      return (isTabRecurring || context.isTabUnconfirmed) && isRecurring ? t("confirm_all") : t("confirm");
288	    case "cancel":
289	      return isTabRecurring && isRecurring ? t("cancel_all_remaining") : t("cancel_event");
290	    case "no_show":
291	      return attendeeList.length === 1 && attendeeList[0].noShow
292	        ? t("unmark_as_no_show")
293	        : t("mark_as_no_show");
294	    case "charge_card":
295	      return cardCharged ? t("no_show_fee_charged") : t("collect_no_show_fee");
296	    default:
297	      return t(actionId);
298	  }
299	}
```

```typescript
/**
 * Builds a public booking page link for the same event type, prefilled with a previous attendee.
 * Shared by the "Book again" booking action and the People view.
 * @returns The relative booking link, or null when the event type can no longer be booked by link
 */
export function buildBookAgainUrl({
  eventType,
  username,
  attendee,
}: {
  eventType: { slug?: string | null; team?: { slug?: string | null } | null } | null | undefined;
  username?: string | null;
  attendee: { name: string; email: string };
}): string | null {
  const slug = eventType?.slug;
  if (!slug) return null;

  const teamSlug = eventType.team?.slug;
  let basePath: string;
  if (teamSlug) {
    basePath = `/team/${teamSlug}/${slug}`;
  } else if (username) {
    basePath = `/${username}/${slug}`;
  } else {
    return null;
  }

  const urlSearchParams = new URLSearchParams({ name: attendee.name, email: attendee.email });
  return `${basePath}?${urlSearchParams.toString()}`;
}

```

```typescript
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { buildBookAgainUrl } from "./buildBookAgainUrl";

const attendee = { name: "John Doe", email: "john@example.com" };

describe("buildBookAgainUrl", () => {
  it("should build a user event link prefilled with the attendee", () => {
    const url = buildBookAgainUrl({
      eventType: { slug: "30min", team: null },
      username: "organizer",
      attendee,
    });

    expect(url).toBe("/organizer/30min?name=John+Doe&email=john%40example.com");
  });

  it("should build a team event link when the event type belongs to a team", () => {
    const url = buildBookAgainUrl({
      eventType: { slug: "sales-call", team: { slug: "acme" } },
      username: "organizer",
      attendee,
    });

    expect(url).toBe("/team/acme/sales-call?name=John+Doe&email=john%40example.com");
  });

  it("should encode special characters in the attendee name and email", () => {
    const url = buildBookAgainUrl({
      eventType: { slug: "30min" },
      username: "organizer",
      attendee: { name: "Zoë & Ana", email: "zoe+test@example.com" },
    });

    const searchParams = new URLSearchParams(url?.split("?")[1]);
    expect(searchParams.get("name")).toBe("Zoë & Ana");
    expect(searchParams.get("email")).toBe("zoe+test@example.com");
  });

  it("should return null when the booking has no event type", () => {
    expect(buildBookAgainUrl({ eventType: null, username: "organizer", attendee })).toBeNull();
  });

  it("should return null when the event type has no slug", () => {
    expect(buildBookAgainUrl({ eventType: { slug: null }, username: "organizer", attendee })).toBeNull();
  });

  it("should return null for a non-team event when the organizer has no username", () => {
    expect(buildBookAgainUrl({ eventType: { slug: "30min" }, username: null, attendee })).toBeNull();
  });
});

```

Book Again (#87) is in place on this branch, and the 11 new tests and the existing booking-action tests pass (69 in total). I haven't committed anything. I also haven't checked it in the running app yet.

**What changed:**
- **New helper** (`apps/web/modules/bookings/lib/buildBookAgainUrl.ts`): it builds the booking-page link for the same event type with the attendee's name and email pre-filled. Team events link to `/team/{team}/{slug}`, others to `/{username}/{slug}`. It returns nothing when there's no event to link to. #88's People view can reuse it.
- **Book again action** (`apps/web/components/booking/actions/bookingActions.ts`): it appears in the "After event" section of a booking's menu, with a `repeat` icon (`calendar-plus` doesn't exist in the icon set). It pre-fills the first attendee, opens a new booking, and leaves the original and Reschedule untouched. It's disabled until the booking has ended, and also when there's no attendee or no link. Cancelled past bookings still get it.
- **Translation:** added `"book_again": "Book again"` to `common.json`.
- **Tests:** 6 for the helper (user event, team event, special characters, three cases with nothing to link to) and 5 for the action in `bookingActions.test.ts`.

**Checks:**
- **Type check:** no errors in the new code. One error remains in `BookingActionsDropdown.tsx` line 410: `requiresRescheduleReason` doesn't exist on the event type. That's from this branch's earlier reschedule-reason work, not this change. The field is in the schema and selected in `get.handler.ts`, so the generated types are probably out of date; `yarn prisma generate` should fix it.
- **Acceptance criterion 4:** I haven't confirmed that the pre-filled name and email can still be edited. The booking form may lock fields that come from the URL. Clicking Book again on a past booking and trying to edit them would settle it.

**To commit:** stage just these four files. `QUIZ-STUDY-NOTES.md` is also untracked and shouldn't go in.

```
git commit -m "feat(bookings): add book again action to past bookings" -m "Closes #87. Part of #51."
```

```text
=== NEW FILE: apps/web/modules/bookings/lib/buildBookAgainUrl.ts ===
/**
 * Builds a public booking page link for the same event type, prefilled with a previous attendee.
 * Shared by the "Book again" booking action and the People view.
 * @returns The relative booking link, or null when the event type can no longer be booked by link
 */
export function buildBookAgainUrl({
  eventType,
  username,
  attendee,
}: {
  eventType: { slug?: string | null; team?: { slug?: string | null } | null } | null | undefined;
  username?: string | null;
  attendee: { name: string; email: string };
}): string | null {
  const slug = eventType?.slug;
  if (!slug) return null;

  const teamSlug = eventType.team?.slug;
  let basePath: string;
  if (teamSlug) {
    basePath = `/team/${teamSlug}/${slug}`;
  } else if (username) {
    basePath = `/${username}/${slug}`;
  } else {
    return null;
  }

  const urlSearchParams = new URLSearchParams({ name: attendee.name, email: attendee.email });
  return `${basePath}?${urlSearchParams.toString()}`;
}
=== NEW FILE: apps/web/modules/bookings/lib/buildBookAgainUrl.test.ts ===
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { buildBookAgainUrl } from "./buildBookAgainUrl";

const attendee = { name: "John Doe", email: "john@example.com" };

describe("buildBookAgainUrl", () => {
  it("should build a user event link prefilled with the attendee", () => {
    const url = buildBookAgainUrl({
      eventType: { slug: "30min", team: null },
      username: "organizer",
      attendee,
    });

    expect(url).toBe("/organizer/30min?name=John+Doe&email=john%40example.com");
  });

  it("should build a team event link when the event type belongs to a team", () => {
    const url = buildBookAgainUrl({
      eventType: { slug: "sales-call", team: { slug: "acme" } },
      username: "organizer",
      attendee,
    });

    expect(url).toBe("/team/acme/sales-call?name=John+Doe&email=john%40example.com");
  });

  it("should encode special characters in the attendee name and email", () => {
    const url = buildBookAgainUrl({
      eventType: { slug: "30min" },
      username: "organizer",
      attendee: { name: "Zoë & Ana", email: "zoe+test@example.com" },
    });

    const searchParams = new URLSearchParams(url?.split("?")[1]);
    expect(searchParams.get("name")).toBe("Zoë & Ana");
    expect(searchParams.get("email")).toBe("zoe+test@example.com");
  });

  it("should return null when the booking has no event type", () => {
    expect(buildBookAgainUrl({ eventType: null, username: "organizer", attendee })).toBeNull();
  });

  it("should return null when the event type has no slug", () => {
    expect(buildBookAgainUrl({ eventType: { slug: null }, username: "organizer", attendee })).toBeNull();
  });

  it("should return null for a non-team event when the organizer has no username", () => {
    expect(buildBookAgainUrl({ eventType: { slug: "30min" }, username: null, attendee })).toBeNull();
  });
});
```
